# _autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md

# learny.tracing.model

The facade: one object that records responses and answers questions about a student.

`LearnerModel` is the thing most callers touch. It owns four collaborators, each one a
constructor argument with a working default, so the simple case needs no arguments at all
and every part can be replaced without touching the others:

| `items`     | what is known about each question (labels, difficulty)                                                                                     |
|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `estimator` | how one response changes belief ([`RaschEstimator`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.estimators.html.md#learny.tracing.estimators.RaschEstimator)) |
| `log`       | the append-only record of responses — the source of truth                                                                                  |
| `estimates` | the cache of per-student state, rebuildable from `log`                                                                                     |

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_CREDIBLE_BELOW`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.DEFAULT_CREDIBLE_BELOW)   | How many posterior standard deviations below its comparator a label must be before [`LearnerModel.weakest()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.weakest) calls it a weakness.   |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`DEFAULT_RELATIVE_TO`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.DEFAULT_RELATIVE_TO)      | the precision-weighted mean of the student's *other* labels, so whatever part of a shortfall every label shares cancels out.                                                      |
| [`DEFAULT_MULTIPLICITY`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.DEFAULT_MULTIPLICITY)     | How the bound accounts for testing several labels at once.                                                                                                                        |

### Classes

| [`LearnerModel`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel)(\*[, items, estimator, log, ...])   | What a student knows, estimated from what they have answered.                                                        |
|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Weakest`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.Weakest)([masteries, reason])                     | What [`LearnerModel.weakest()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.weakest) returns: a list of `Mastery`, plus why. |

### learny.tracing.model.DEFAULT_CREDIBLE_BELOW *= 1.0*

How many posterior standard deviations below its comparator a label must be before
[`LearnerModel.weakest()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.weakest) calls it a weakness. 1.0 is a one-sided ~84% credible
bound. With the default `multiplicity="calibrated"` (and `"bonferroni"`) it is the
bound for the *whole set* of labels tested — a student with no real weakness gets a
label flagged about one time in six at most, however many labels there are — and with
`multiplicity="none"` it is per label. It stops a set of labels that never vary independently (many labels on every
item) from being ranked at all. Raise it when a false “practise this” is costly.

### learny.tracing.model.DEFAULT_MULTIPLICITY *= 'calibrated'*

How the bound accounts for testing several labels at once. `"calibrated"` raises the
per-label z as Bonferroni does, so the chance of *any* false flag is about
`1 - Phi(credible_below)`, and measures each label against how far its contrast
would wander with no real weakness ([`Mastery.null_var`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.estimators.html.md#learny.tracing.estimators.Mastery.null_var)) rather than against its posterior sd,
which a shrunk posterior mean stays well inside (#22). `"bonferroni"` does the same
on the posterior sd: a bound rather than a calibration, far below its target with
little evidence, so it costs power at cold start. `"none"` applies
`credible_below` to each label separately, as the original gate did.

### learny.tracing.model.DEFAULT_RELATIVE_TO *= 'labels'*

the precision-weighted mean
of the student’s *other* labels, so whatever part of a shortfall every label shares
cancels out. `"global"`: the student’s global skill (zero deviation), as the
original gate did.
With `"labels"` a student with evidence on a single label has nothing to compare it
with, so nothing is credibly weak.

* **Type:**
  What a label’s weakness is measured against. `"labels"`

### *class* learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel(, items=None, estimator=None, log=None, estimates=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

What a student knows, estimated from what they have answered.

```pycon
>>> items = {
...     'q1': Item('q1', labels=('fractions',), difficulty=0.25),
...     'q2': Item('q2', labels=('fractions', 'area'), difficulty=0.75),
... }
>>> model = LearnerModel(items=items, log={}, estimates={})
>>> round(model.predict('ada', 'q2'), 3)  # no data: near the item's own pass rate
0.286
>>> model.record('ada', 'q1', 'correct')
>>> model.record('ada', 'q2', 'wrong')
>>> 0.0 < model.predict('ada', 'q2') < 1.0
True
>>> sorted(model.mastery('ada'))
['area', 'fractions']
```

Getting a hard item wrong should leave the student looking weaker on the labels it
exercises than a student who has answered nothing:

```pycon
>>> model.mastery('ada')['area'].mu < model.mastery('ada')['fractions'].mu
True
```

#### calibration(students=None, , n_bins=10)

Prequential calibration over the log; see [`calibration()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.calibration).

Reads the log only; the estimate cache is neither used nor changed. With an
estimator that reads scores, scored responses are left to
[`score_calibration()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.score_calibration), so a log of scores alone gives an empty report here.

* **Return type:**
  [`CalibrationReport`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.diagnostics.html.md#learny.tracing.diagnostics.CalibrationReport)

#### mastery(student)

Per-label mastery for one student, weakest first when sorted by skill.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Mastery`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.estimators.html.md#learny.tracing.estimators.Mastery)]

#### predict(student, item)

Probability that `student` answers `item` correctly.

* **Return type:**
  [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)

#### record(student, item, outcome, , at=None, score=None, max_score=None, \*\*meta)

Log one response and fold it into the student’s estimate.

The log is written first: if updating the cache fails, the evidence survives and
[`replay()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.replay) can rebuild from it. `score` out of `max_score` records an
ordered score alongside the right/wrong `outcome` (see
[`Response`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.Response)); the default estimator reads only the
outcome, [`PartialCreditEstimator`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.estimators.html.md#learny.tracing.estimators.PartialCreditEstimator) the score.

```pycon
>>> from learny.tracing.estimators import PartialCreditEstimator
>>> items = {'song-7/tempo': Item('song-7/tempo', labels=('tempo',))}
>>> model = LearnerModel(
...     items=items, estimator=PartialCreditEstimator(), log={}, estimates={}
... )
>>> model.record('ada', 'song-7/tempo', 'correct', score=4, max_score=4)
>>> model.mastery('ada')['tempo'].mu > 0
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### record_many(responses)

Record a batch — a whole paper, say — in the order given.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### replay(student=None)

Rebuild estimates from the log, discarding the cache.

This is what makes changing the estimator a re-run rather than a migration, and
it is asserted by the tests: folding `observe` over the log must reproduce the
state that live recording produced.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### score_calibration(students=None, , n_bins=10)

Prequential calibration of the score forecasts; see [`score_calibration()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.score_calibration).

Reads the log only. Needs an estimator that reads scores, such as
[`PartialCreditEstimator`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.estimators.html.md#learny.tracing.estimators.PartialCreditEstimator).

* **Return type:**
  [`ScoreCalibrationReport`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.diagnostics.html.md#learny.tracing.diagnostics.ScoreCalibrationReport)

#### separation(student, , threshold=2.0)

How distinguishable this student’s labels are; see `label_separation()`.

Check `.distinguishable` before acting on an ordering from [`weakest()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.weakest).

* **Return type:**
  [`LabelSeparation`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.diagnostics.html.md#learny.tracing.diagnostics.LabelSeparation)

#### weakest(student, n=5, , credible_below=1.0, relative_to='labels', multiplicity='calibrated')

The labels this student is credibly weakest on — what to practise next.

By default a label is returned only when it is credibly below the student’s
*other* labels: the upper bound `c + z * sd` of its contrast `c` — its
`Mastery.deviation` minus the
precision-weighted mean deviation of every other label with evidence — is below
zero. The survivors are ranked by posterior mean mastery, worst first, and the
first `n` returned.

Three keywords set the gate:

* `credible_below` — the z of the bound (default [`DEFAULT_CREDIBLE_BELOW`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.DEFAULT_CREDIBLE_BELOW),
  ~84% one-sided); larger `z` demands more certainty. With
  `multiplicity="none"`, `z = 0` keeps every label merely below its
  comparator on average. `None` switches the gate off and ranks every
  label with evidence by posterior mean — check [`separation()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.separation) before
  believing that ranking.
* `multiplicity` — `"calibrated"` (default) corrects for testing every label
  with evidence at once, so `z` sets the chance of *any* false flag (about
  one student in six with no real weakness, at `z = 1`), and measures each
  contrast against its sampling spread under no real weakness
  ([`Mastery.null_var`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.estimators.html.md#learny.tracing.estimators.Mastery.null_var)) and
  skew (a rare wrong answer from a student who is usually right is a large
  drop), so the correction costs little power at cold start (#22). An estimator that does
  not fill `null_var` gets `"bonferroni"` (a label it leaves unfilled is
  measured by its posterior spread): the same correction on the posterior sd, which shrinkage already makes cautious when evidence is thin, so
  with a few responses per label even a large real weakness is rarely returned.
  `"none"` applies `z` to each label separately, which with six labels, a few
  hundred responses and no real weakness flags something more often than not.
  Under `relative_to="global"` the calibrated spread is more cautious (the
  part of a label’s spread it shares with the others is counted, not removed).
  A label stored before null spreads were tracked is measured by its posterior
  spread until it is answered again.
* `relative_to` — `"labels"` (default) as above; `"global"` measures each
  label’s deviation against zero, the student’s global skill. The default
  estimator carries the global/label covariance, so a shortfall every item
  shares goes to the global skill, and where the record cannot tell “weak
  overall” from “weak on this label” the label’s deviation stays wide rather
  than taking the blame (#23); the contrast with the other labels counts the
  covariance they share through it ([`Mastery.loading`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.estimators.html.md#learny.tracing.estimators.Mastery.loading)). Evidence on a single label is
  never a credible weakness under `"labels"` — there is nothing to compare it
  with. When unlabelled items carry the comparison (a label against the rest of
  the paper), use `"global"`.

`multiplicity="none", relative_to="global"` restores the original per-label gate.

Labels with no evidence are never included: the model has nothing to say about
them, and saying it anyway is how a learner model loses trust.

**An empty answer is common and says why.** The result is a list (a
[`Weakest`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.Weakest)) whose `reason` is `None` when it holds labels, and
otherwise one of:

* `"no_evidence"` — the student has answered nothing that carries a label;
* `"no_credible_weakness"` — there is evidence, but no label is credibly
  below the rest of the student’s record. That is a statement about *relative*
  weakness, not “nothing to practise”: practise at the student’s overall level
  (`model.estimator.skill(state)` for the default estimator).

Raises `ValueError` for a negative `credible_below` (which would admit labels
credibly *above* their comparator) or an unknown `relative_to` /
`multiplicity`, and `TypeError` when the gate is on but
the estimator’s [`Mastery`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.estimators.html.md#learny.tracing.estimators.Mastery) values carry no
`deviation` — rather than silently returning nothing.

```pycon
>>> items = {f'q{i}': Item(f'q{i}', labels=('area' if i % 2 else 'sums',))
...          for i in range(40)}
>>> model = LearnerModel(items=items, log={}, estimates={})
>>> model.weakest('ada')
[]
>>> model.weakest('ada').reason
'no_evidence'
>>> for i in range(40):  # right on every sum, wrong on every area question
...     model.record('ada', f'q{i}', 'wrong' if i % 2 else 'correct')
>>> [m.label for m in model.weakest('ada')]
['area']
>>> [m.label for m in model.weakest('ada', credible_below=None)]  # plain ranking
['area', 'sums']
>>> [m.label for m in model.weakest('ada', relative_to='global', multiplicity='none')]
['area']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Weakest`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.Weakest)

### *class* learny.tracing.model.Weakest(masteries=(), , reason=None)

Bases: [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)

What [`LearnerModel.weakest()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.weakest) returns: a list of `Mastery`, plus why.

It *is* a list — it compares, iterates, slices and serialises like one — so callers
that treat the result as a list keep working. `reason` is `None` when the list is
non-empty and says why it is empty otherwise; see [`LearnerModel.weakest()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.model.html.md#learny.tracing.model.LearnerModel.weakest). It
describes the answer as returned: slicing gives a plain list, and a caller that
mutates the result owns keeping `reason` meaningful.

```pycon
>>> w = Weakest(reason='no_evidence')
>>> w == [], w.reason
(True, 'no_evidence')
```


# _autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md

# learny.tracing.records

Core data types for learner modelling: items, outcomes, and responses.

These are the vocabulary every other module in [`learny.tracing`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.html.md#module-learny.tracing) speaks. They are
deliberately small and serialisable: a [`Response`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.Response) is what gets appended to the
append-only log that is the system’s single source of truth, so its shape is a
long-lived commitment while everything derived from it is a rebuildable cache.

The three-valued [`Outcome`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.Outcome) is not an accident. Many assessments distinguish a
wrong answer from an unanswered one — competition scoring often rewards prudent
abstention — so collapsing `SKIPPED` into `WRONG` destroys signal at the point of
capture, where it can never be recovered. Estimators decide what to do with a skip;
the log records what happened.

### Module Attributes

| [`LabelWeights`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.LabelWeights)   | A mapping from label to the weight that label carries for an item.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Functions

| [`restrict_labels`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.restrict_labels)(items, \*, keep[, ...])   | Project an item bank onto a subset of its labels — one facet, say.   |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### Classes

| [`Outcome`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.Outcome)(\*values)                                 | What happened when a student met an item.                                   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`Item`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.Item)(id[, labels, difficulty, meta])              | A question, with the skill labels it exercises and its observed difficulty. |
| [`Response`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.Response)(student, item, outcome[, at, meta, ...]) | One student meeting one item, once.                                         |

### *class* learny.tracing.records.Item(id, labels=(), difficulty=None, meta=dict())

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

A question, with the skill labels it exercises and its observed difficulty.

`labels` is this item’s row of the Q-matrix: which knowledge components the item
draws on. `difficulty` is an *externally observed* difficulty on the unit
interval — the proportion of a reference population expected to get it wrong — and
is the strongest prior available before a given student has answered anything.
Leave it `None` when nothing observed is available.

```pycon
>>> item = Item("2004-q7", labels=("fractions", "area"), difficulty=0.4)
>>> item.weights
{'fractions': 1.0, 'area': 1.0}
>>> Item("q1", labels={"fractions": 0.85, "traps": 0.57}).weights["traps"]
0.57
```

#### *property* weights *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [float](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]*

Labels as a `{label: weight}` mapping, whichever form they were given in.

### learny.tracing.records.LabelWeights

A mapping from label to the weight that label carries for an item. Weights are
usually 1.0 (the label applies) but may be attenuated — by a facet’s measured
inter-rater reliability, for instance — so that a noisily-assigned label moves a
mastery estimate less than a reliably-assigned one.

alias of [`Mapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.Mapping)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`float`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#float)]

### *class* learny.tracing.records.Outcome(\*values)

Bases: [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Enum`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/enum.html#enum.Enum)

What happened when a student met an item.

`str`-valued so it serialises to JSON as itself, with no encoder needed:

```pycon
>>> import json
>>> json.dumps({"status": Outcome.CORRECT})
'{"status": "correct"}'
>>> Outcome("wrong") is Outcome.WRONG
True
```

#### *property* is_scored *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

Whether this outcome carries evidence about ability.

A skip is evidence about *confidence or time*, not about whether the student
could have answered, so estimators are entitled to ignore it.

```pycon
>>> [o.is_scored for o in Outcome]
[True, True, False]
```

### *class* learny.tracing.records.Response(student, item, outcome, at=None, meta=dict(), , score=None, max_score=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

One student meeting one item, once. The unit of the append-only log.

`at` is a POSIX timestamp. It is kept because order and elapsed time are what any
later model of forgetting will need, and a log that did not record it cannot be
replayed into one.

```pycon
>>> r = Response("cora", "2004-q7", Outcome.CORRECT, at=1_700_000_000.0)
>>> r.correct
True
>>> Response.from_dict(r.to_dict()) == r
True
```

**An ordered score** — 1 to 5 stars, partial credit — goes in `score` out of
`max_score`, on the consecutive levels `0..max_score`: map 1–5 stars to
`score=stars - 1, max_score=4`, and three ordered levels such as 1/3/5 stars to
`0, 1, 2` of `2` (a level that can never occur is not a level). `outcome` stays
the dichotomous view of the same attempt, so an estimator that only reads outcomes
(the default) is unaffected, and one that reads scores
([`PartialCreditEstimator`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.estimators.html.md#learny.tracing.estimators.PartialCreditEstimator)) can replay the same log.
One response carries one score: an attempt scored on several sub-scales is several
responses, one per sub-scale.

```pycon
>>> r = Response("cora", "song-7/tempo", "correct", score=3, max_score=4)
>>> r.to_dict()['score'], Response.from_dict(r.to_dict()) == r
(3, True)
>>> 'score' in Response("cora", "2004-q7", "correct").to_dict()  # unscored: as before
False
>>> Response("cora", "q", "skipped", score=0, max_score=4)
Traceback (most recent call last):
    ...
ValueError: Response 'q': a skipped response has no score (got score=0)
```

#### *property* correct *: [bool](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#bool)*

True only for an outright correct answer; a skip is not a correct answer.

#### *classmethod* from_dict(d)

Inverse of [`to_dict()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.Response.to_dict), tolerant of unknown keys from a future version.

* **Return type:**
  [`Response`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.Response)

#### max_score *: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

The highest score this attempt could have earned; set exactly when `score` is.

#### score *: [int](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int) | [None](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)* *= None*

The ordered score, in `0..max_score`; `None` for a right/wrong response.

#### to_dict()

A JSON-ready dict. `Outcome` is a `str` enum, so it needs no encoding.

An unscored response leaves `score` and `max_score` out, so a right/wrong log
is written exactly as it was before scores existed.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### learny.tracing.records.restrict_labels(items, , keep, drop_unlabelled=False)

Project an item bank onto a subset of its labels — one facet, say.

Labels that never vary independently of each other cannot be told apart: tag every
item with nine labels and each label’s deviation stays at the student’s global
skill, whatever the data. Modelling one facet at a time is often what makes labels
separable ([`label_separation()`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.diagnostics.html.md#learny.tracing.diagnostics.label_separation) measures it).
*Which* labels belong together is a judgement about the taxonomy, so the library
never collapses anything by itself; this is the explicit, opt-in way to do it.

`keep` is a collection of labels or a predicate on a label. Weights are preserved.
An item left with no labels still carries its difficulty and still informs the
student’s global skill, so it is kept unless `drop_unlabelled=True`.

```pycon
>>> bank = {
...     'q1': Item('q1', labels={'topic:fractions': 1.0, 'trap:units': 0.6}),
...     'q2': Item('q2', labels=('trap:units',), difficulty=0.7),
... }
>>> topics = restrict_labels(bank, keep=lambda label: label.startswith('topic:'))
>>> topics['q1'].weights, topics['q2'].weights, topics['q2'].difficulty
({'topic:fractions': 1.0}, {}, 0.7)
>>> sorted(restrict_labels(bank, keep={'topic:fractions'}, drop_unlabelled=True))
['q1']
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Item`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.records.html.md#learny.tracing.records.Item)]


# _autosummary/learny.tracing.stores.html.md

# learny.tracing.stores

Where learner data lives, and how code reaches it.

Two stores, both plain `MutableMapping` so the backend is configuration rather than
code: swapping local JSON files for S3 (`s3dol`) or a database is an argument, not a
rewrite.

The default root is `~/.local/share/learny/` — deliberately **not** inside the package
or any app directory. Per-student responses are personal data and mutable runtime state;
a store that defaulted to `./data` would invite every caller to commit it. Override the
root for the whole package with the `LEARNY_DATA_DIR` environment variable, which is
what tests and CI should set.

### Functions

| [`data_dir`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.stores.html.md#learny.tracing.stores.data_dir)([kind, app_name])    | The per-kind data directory, created on demand.                     |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`response_log`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.stores.html.md#learny.tracing.stores.response_log)(\*[, rootdir])   | The default response log, under `~/.local/share/learny/responses/`. |
| [`estimate_store`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.stores.html.md#learny.tracing.stores.estimate_store)(\*[, rootdir]) | Per-student mastery estimates, keyed by student.                    |

### Classes

| [`ResponseLog`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.stores.html.md#learny.tracing.stores.ResponseLog)(\*[, rootdir])   | The append-only record of every response.   |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|

### *class* learny.tracing.stores.ResponseLog(, rootdir=None)

Bases: [`object`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#object)

The append-only record of every response. The single source of truth.

One JSON-lines file per student, so one student’s data can be handed over, audited
or deleted on its own — which matters when the data is a child’s.

Append-only is not fastidiousness: the estimator *will* change, and a log that can
be replayed is what makes changing it a re-run rather than a migration.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile
>>> from learny.tracing.records import Response, Outcome
>>> log = ResponseLog(rootdir=tempfile.mkdtemp())
>>> log.append(Response('ada', 'q1', Outcome.CORRECT, at=1.0))
>>> log.append(Response('ada', 'q2', Outcome.SKIPPED, at=2.0))
>>> log.append(Response('bob', 'q1', Outcome.WRONG, at=1.5))
>>> sorted(log.students())
['ada', 'bob']
>>> [r.item for r in log['ada']]
['q1', 'q2']
>>> len(list(log))
3
```

#### append(response)

Append one response. Never rewrites or reorders what is already there.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### extend(responses)

Append many responses, grouped so each student’s file is opened once.

* **Return type:**
  [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

#### students()

Every student with at least one logged response.

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]

### learny.tracing.stores.data_dir(kind='', , app_name='learny')

The per-kind data directory, created on demand.

Resolution order: the `LEARNY_DATA_DIR` environment variable, then
`config2py.AppData` if it is installed (which gets Windows right), then the XDG
default. Data is always written under a *kind* subfolder so the root stays free for
kinds that do not exist yet.

```pycon
>>> import tempfile, os
>>> os.environ['LEARNY_DATA_DIR'] = tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp()
>>> data_dir('responses') == Path(tmp) / 'responses'
True
>>> data_dir('responses').is_dir()
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Path`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/pathlib.html#pathlib.Path)

### learny.tracing.stores.estimate_store(, rootdir=None)

Per-student mastery estimates, keyed by student.

This is a **cache**. Anything in here can be thrown away and rebuilt by replaying
the response log, and the tests assert exactly that.

* **Return type:**
  [`MutableMapping`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/collections.abc.html#collections.abc.MutableMapping)

### learny.tracing.stores.response_log(, rootdir=None)

The default response log, under `~/.local/share/learny/responses/`.

* **Return type:**
  [`ResponseLog`](_autosummary/learny.tracing.stores.html.md#learny.tracing.stores.ResponseLog)

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`learny` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `learning-game-patterns`

A pattern language for games that teach symbols (characters of another script) and vocabulary: the ten learning families (match, produce, construct, order, discriminate, context, explore, encode, schedule, assess), the six matching patterns (pick-the-match, pair-off field, hidden pair, route the stream, find in a field, chain), nine pressure renderings (countdown bar, falling object, overflow container, time bank, and more), and which to use in which learning phase. Use when designing or choosing a mechanic for a language-learning, kana, kanji, alphabet or vocabulary game, when asked “what kinds of matching games are there”, “how should the timer work”, “which game form for look-alike characters”, or when deciding what a game must log for the learner model.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/learny learning-game-patterns --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`skills/learning-game-patterns`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/learny/tree/HEAD/skills/learning-game-patterns).

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`.claude/CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/learny/tree/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/learny/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`learny.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/learny/learny.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/learny/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
